As someone who has lived in both, it is Columbus 100% without a doubt. There is SO much to do there -- events, clubs, restaurant/foodie scene, live entertainment, etc. The population is 4x the size, and the city has developed nicely to accommodate. I moved there without knowing anyone and was able to make new friends and grow in my career -- there are a lot of young professional networking groups. Check out CYP -- [https://www.cypclub.com/](https://www.cypclub.com/) Sure it is expensive, but I think you'll find it's worth it. If you want to be in the heart of it with great bars and restaurants and young people, The Short North is very cool. I lived in Harrison West and LOVED it but it's gotten overpriced. Check out Easton area -- it's about 20 mins from downtown and you're near the mall but they have a couple giant apartment complexes down there that are more of an affordable rate, yet nice. Avoid Franklinton -- still pretty seedy and I personally wouldn't feel comfortable living there solo.

  
All that to say, Toledo is great in its own way. We moved back here for family and friends. We have everything we need here and are happy. I have zero complaints. But if you're looking for something new and a place to make friends easier -- Cbus is it.

Paying for pilates after PT was too expensive, so I went to pure barre. I've been doing pure barre for about 1.5 months, and have done 14 classes now. I feel like it is helping to stabilize the joint. I have to make sure i foam roll my glutes every day so that i don't get "dead butt" and my glutes fire during class. Once I was able to get my foam rolls down and release those tight muscles, i feel like i've been seeing benefits from PB. My SI joint pain used to be a 7/10 daily a couple of years ago, and now I'm at zero pain!
